before.abstract: Trained action policies write manipulation skill into network weights, tying what is learned to the distribution it is learned from. In-context learning (ICL) avoids this coupling but has not matched trained policies, because a demonstration recorded in another scene carries no feedback from the world the robot currently faces. We observe that what an agent learns in context is semantic, recording task steps and object roles rather than visual appearance, so experience gathered in one world transfers to another. Based on this insight, we propose World In-Context Learning (WICL), a paradigm in which a frozen model starts from a demonstration, rehearses the task in a world such as a simulator, and writes the feedback into its context rather than its weights. We build RoboScript, a modular infrastructure that implements WICL for agentic manipulation. From a single demonstration, RoboScript learns each task through rehearsal in simulation, freezes the learned knowledge as a Task Memory, and deploys the frozen memory on new scenes with data isolation that ensures every deployment input is available on a real robot. On all 50 tasks of RoboTwin 2.0, RoboScript reaches 83.4% mean success across clean and randomized settings with one demonstration per task and no gradient updates, exceeding the strongest trained action policy by over 20 points. The method generalizes across visual distributions, improves through reflection, scales with the foundation model, and transfers to a physical dual-arm robot through cross-embodiment memory adaptation. With a world in the loop, a robot can learn a manipulation task in its context as well as it learns one in its weights. All code is available at https://github.com/ArcheOne-AI/RoboScript

review.note: RoboScript 的§4.1有独立Harness证据：coding agent为动作接口缺口写可复用skills，driver执行原场景与其他布局验证，循环到coverage停止提升后冻结，供Agent后续任务学习与部署调用。Task Memory及反思仍须另标经验内容，不将整篇所有记忆都算Harness。 逐项证据、分歧与纠正保留于 docs/internal/reports/maintenance-2026-11-11/。不声称复算全部论文数字。

summary_override.summary_en: Before task learning, RoboScript segments the collected demonstrations and asks a coding agent to write environment-specific skills for gaps in the existing action interface. An independent driver replays the skills, checks transfer across layouts, and rechecks gains against regressions. Coverage feedback drives further rounds before the skill library is frozen for later tasks. Inclusion is limited to this executable tool-skill construction and selection loop, separate from ordinary Task Memory content updates. The paper does not isolate the contribution of skill construction, and continual failure-driven skill creation during deployment remains future work.
summary_override.summary_zh: RoboScript 在任务学习前把汇集的示范拆为动作片段，将现有接口无法覆盖的缺口交给 coding agent 编写环境技能。独立 driver 回放、检查跨布局复用并复查新增技能的得失，按覆盖反馈迭代后冻结技能库，供后续任务调用。这里仅将可执行工具技能的构建与筛选闭环纳入 Harness；普通 Task Memory 内容更新另计。论文未单独量化技能构建的贡献，部署中遇到失败再持续生成新技能仍是未来工作。

before.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
